WireGuard is now spelled out across the management-plane surface: `minds-admin wg` is `minds-admin wireguard` (`wg` remains a hidden alias), `--via-wg` is `--via-wireguard`, and the renderer/prep/DB identifiers (`wireguard_address`, `wireguard_public_key`, the prep marker `MNGR_WIREGUARD_PUBLIC_KEY`, ...) match. WireGuard's own surface (`wg`/`wg-quick` binaries, `wg0`, `/etc/wireguard` paths, config syntax) is untouched.

Operator tooling now reaches locked-down boxes over the WireGuard overlay: every box-management SSH (bake, prep, drain/destroy/teardown, occupancy audit, CI slice sweep, warm-cache, repair-keys, backfill-host-keys, wireguard sync-peers) resolves its dial address through a shared resolver -- the box's overlay address when a sub-second probe shows the operator's tunnel reaches it, else the public address. This unblocks restocking a pool whose box `:22` lockdown is live (the dev canary's exact failure); `wireguard sync-peers --via-wireguard` becomes a force-overlay override rather than a requirement (and is since removed entirely).

The dial resolver now prefers a **userspace WireGuard tunnel** (onetun): when the onetun binary and the operator's private key (`~/.minds-wireguard/<tier>.key`, or `MINDS_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH`) are available, box-management SSH rides a per-box local forward speaking the WireGuard protocol in-process -- no root, no network interface, no local peer list (the peer is built from the box's DB row per dial), verified end to end via the box sshd's banner. Kernel-route overlay dials and the public address remain the fallbacks, and `wg-quick` is only needed for interactive box SSH.

Management overlays are now per-tier disjoint carves of a reserved `10.64.0.0/10` supernet (production `10.64.0.0/11`; staging/ci/dev `10.96.0.0/16`, `10.104.0.0/16`, `10.112.0.0/16`, each at the base of a reserved /13 for one-value 8x growth), replacing the single `10.202.0.0/16` every tier reused -- several tiers' tunnels can now coexist on one operator machine. A box stamped outside its tier's current allocation is renumbered at its next prep.
